The RES (Relative Error Score) serves as a core metric to validate eligibility for ranking and publishing. When RES exceeds a Brier-cap threshold, the system enters a selective mode that adjusts blending weights (0.7/0.3) to reduce overconfidence. A ranking pause is triggered when RES stabilizes above 0.02, indicating sufficient signal strength but avoiding premature convergence. This mechanism ensures that performance statistics are only published when confidence thresholds are met, aligning with a Bayesian approach to probabilistic forecasting. Failure modes include Brier score inflation due to insufficient data or misalignment between independent and live signals. The system avoids flipping flags like AUTO_PUBLISH unless RES and Brier metrics converge, maintaining integrity through calibration and telemetry.
